emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(sk->sk_state)]) from thread_a (the first, lockless evaluation of the sk_wait_event condition must not interleave with a conflicting write)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@tcp_disconnect = mutate(sk->sk_state) during disconnect/shutdown state transition
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_b changes sk_state while holding the socket lock, but sk_wait_event evaluates its condition locklessly first (the waiter has not serialized this read under the socket lock); one-sided lock does not serialize the lockless condition read → no g establishes atomic(read)
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single access (an unmarked lockless condition read concurrent with a conflicting write) → data race

fix_maps_to: READ_ONCE() wrapped around the lockless sk_wait_event condition reads of sk_state/sk_err/sk_shutdown/sk_write_pending in sk_stream_wait_connect and sibling waiters (SMC/LLC/TIPC/TLS/BPF) → marks the read as a single well-defined access (establishes atomic(read) at the C-memory-model level)
recall_risk_notes: Same one-sided-lock condition-read family as the copied_seq race; unprotected reader yields atomic(read) directly and threads/object (sendmsg vs disconnect on struct sock::sk_state) are static-friendly. Risks: (1) benign word read inside a wait condition — an LLM may judge it benign and decline to assert atomic(read); (2) the read site is buried inside the sk_wait_event MACRO expansion, so resolving the exact conflicting line/op may be fragile for grounding; (3) the writer's exact sk_state write line in tcp_disconnect is unspecified (line 0) and reached via tcp_set_state.
